take.title: The Card and the Atlas
take.bookTitle: The making of the LEGO Odyssey

segments.speaker: examiner
segments.caption: Before the bricks there was another film, drawn in dots on paper. It was called the halfworld.

segments.speaker: examiner
segments.caption: Its first commit: the twenty-third of July, at six minutes to three in the morning. Four hundred and ninety-four files at once.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.caption: And with them, a card. Paste this into Claude, with any book. The film is the program.

segments.speaker: director
segments.caption: What does the card ask for?

segments.speaker: agent
segments.caption: First the atlas: every book broken into scenes, every scene into beats, each beat causing the next. Then one engine. Then the drawings.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.caption: Every figure is a small program that draws itself in flat tone. One last pass prints the frame as dots on a grid, as Knowlton's films were made at Bell Labs in 1963.

segments.speaker: examiner
segments.caption: Fifteen books were already in that first commit: three hundred and seven drawings, ninety-four scenes. How they were made before it, the record does not say.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.caption: The card says how. Build a few, verify, then fan out.

segments.speaker: agent
segments.caption: To many of me, at once.
